text:
eli: Quick policy check from our Lisbon trip -- asked whether I should use per-diem for meals or submit receipts. Also rented a car and returned it with half tank; receipt for fuel missing (paid at roadside). Any preferred way to file these?
people-ops: Hi @eli 12; short: per-diem is available for domestic US trips only (per current policy). For international travel you must submit receipts for meals unless your trip qualifies for a special per-diem waiver (rare).
eli: Ah got it. This was a EMEA trip so I'll attach receipts. But the roadside fuel slip is tiny and smudged. Will that be okay?
finance-sam: We accept smudged/mutilated receipts if the merchant, date, and amount are legible. If info missing, add a note with: origin, destination, date and miles driven, and approximate amount. Example note: "Fuel refill, A23 roadside, 2026-02-12, ~€32 (no legible slip)".
eli: If I don't have a fuel receipt at all (lost), can I claim a reasonable estimate?
finance-sam: Lost receipts: manager approval required and we may ask for a GPS log or trip record. Put the estimate as a line item flagged "lost receipt" and attach manager approval in expensify.
manager-zoe: I can approve a one-off estimate for Eli's claim if they add the trip note and the rental agreement.
eli: thanks Zoe, will attach agreement + note. Also one more: incidental snacks on late flights where I only have a screenshot from the airline app. Is that fine?
people-ops: Screenshots from an airline app are acceptable if they show date, merchant, and amount. For card statement-only evidence, include the statement line.
expensify-bot: Reminder: tag expenses with project code, attach one file per receipt, mark any "lost receipt" items with manager approval. Claims submitted before 17:00 PT processed within 3 business days.
eli: Perfect. I'll submit with notes and manager approval now :thumbsup:
